definition.name: Tough
definition.description:
Origin Feat

Your Hit Point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your character level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a character level thereafter, your Hit Point maximum increases by an additional 2 Hit Points.
definition.snippet: When you take this feat, your HP maximum increases by {{2*characterlevel}}. Whenever you gain a character level thereafter, your HP maximum increases an additional 2 HP.

definition.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
definition.description:
Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

When you make an extra attack as a result of using a weapon that has the Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren’t already adding it to the damage.
definition.snippet: When you make an extra attack as a result of using a weapon that has the Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren’t already adding it to the damage.

definition.name: Unarmed Fighting
definition.description:
Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

When you hit with your Unarmed Strike and deal damage, you can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike. If you aren’t holding any weapons or a Shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8.

At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 Bludgeoning damage to one creature Grappled by you.

definition.name: Runestones
definition.description: At the beginning of the Northlands Sagas adventure path, each player should draw one Runestone randomly.
definition.snippet: At the beginning of the Northlands Sagas adventure path, each player should draw one Runestone randomly.

definition.name: Arcane Infiltrator
definition.description:
Origin Feat

You gain the following benefits.

Cantrip. You learn the Friends cantrip. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this feat).

Cunning Diversion. You can take the Dodge action as a Bonus Action. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
definition.snippet:
Cantrip. You learn the Friends cantrip. Int., Wis., or Cha. is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this feat).

definition.name: Guidance
definition.description: You touch a willing creature and choose a skill. Until the spell ends, the creature adds 1d4 to any ability check using the chosen skill.

definition.name: Light
definition.description:
You touch one Large or smaller object that isn’t being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

definition.name: Bane
definition.description:
Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within range must each make a Charisma saving throw. Whenever a target that fails this save makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract 1d4 from the attack roll or save.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

definition.name: Poison Spray
definition.description:
You spray toxic mist at a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d12 Poison damage.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d12 when you reach levels 5 (2d12), 11 (3d12), and 17 (4d12).

definition.name: Starry Wisp
definition.description:
You launch a mote of light at one creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 Radiant damage, and until the end of your next turn, it emits Dim Light in a 10-foot radius and can’t benefit from the Invisible condition.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

definition.name: Charm Person
definition.description:
One Humanoid you can see within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. It does so with Advantage if you or your allies are fighting it. On a failed save, the target has the Charmed condition until the spell ends or until you or your allies damage it. The Charmed creature is Friendly to you. When the spell ends, the target knows it was Charmed by you.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

conditions.exception: Spell duration or until harmful action

definition.name: Acid Splash
definition.description:
You create an acidic bubble at a point within range, where it explodes in a 5-foot-radius Sphere. Each creature in that Sphere must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 Acid damage.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6).

definition.name: Fire Bolt
definition.description:
You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or an object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell starts burning if it isn’t being worn or carried.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d10 when you reach levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10).

definition.name: Chromatic Orb
definition.description:
You hurl an orb of energy at a target within range. Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder for the type of orb you create, and then make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 3d8 damage of the chosen type.

If you roll the same number on two or more of the d8s, the orb leaps to a different target of your choice within 30 feet of the target. Make an attack roll against the new target, and make a new damage roll. The orb can’t leap again unless you cast the spell with a level 2+ spell slot.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1. The orb can leap a maximum number of times equal to the level of the slot expended, and a creature can be targeted only once by each casting of this spell.

definition.name: Bait and Switch
definition.description:
When you’re within 5 feet of a creature on your turn, you can expend one superiority die and switch places with that creature, provided you spend at least 5 feet of movement and the creature is willing and isn’t incapacitated. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

Roll the superiority die. Until the start of your next turn, you or the other creature (your choice) gains a bonus to AC equal to the number rolled.

definition.name: Goading Attack
definition.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to goad the target into attacking you. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls against targets other than you until the end of your next turn.

On failure, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls against targets other than you until the end of your next turn.

options.label: Activate Rage
options.description:
While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

No Concentration or Spells. You can’t maintain Concentration, and you can’t cast spells.

Duration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

  • Make an attack roll against an enemy.
  • Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
  • Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.

Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.

options.label: Commander’s Strike
options.description: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can forgo one of your attacks and use a bonus action to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you and expend one superiority die. That creature can immediately use its reaction to make one weapon attack, adding the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll.

options.label: Disarming Attack
options.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to disarm the target, forcing it to drop one item of your choice that it’s holding. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and the target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it drops the object you choose. The object lands at its feet.

options.label: Distracting Strike
options.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to distract the creature, giving your allies an opening. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll. The next attack roll against the target by an attacker other than you has advantage if the attack is made before the start of your next turn.

options.label: Evasive Footwork
options.description: When you move, you can expend one superiority die, rolling the die and adding the number rolled to your AC until you stop moving.

options.label: Feinting Attack
options.description: You can expend one superiority die and use a bonus action on your turn to feint, choosing one creature within 5 feet of you as your target. You have advantage on your next attack roll against that creature this turn. If that attack hits, add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll.

options.label: Lunging Attack
options.description: When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, you can expend one superiority die to increase your reach for that attack by 5 feet. If you hit, you add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll.

options.label: Maneuvering Attack
options.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to maneuver one of your comrades into a more advantageous position. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and you choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from the target of your attack.

options.label: Menacing Attack
options.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to frighten the target. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

options.label: Parry
options.description: When another creature damages you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction and expend one superiority die to reduce the damage by the number you roll on your superiority die + your Dexterity modifier.

options.label: Precision Attack
options.description: When you make a weapon attack roll against a creature, you can expend one superiority die to add it to the roll. You can use this maneuver before or after making the attack roll, but before any effects of the attack are applied.

options.label: Pushing Attack
options.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to drive the target back. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and if the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you push the target up to 15 feet away from you.

options.label: Rally
options.description: On your turn, you can use a bonus action and expend one superiority die to bolster the resolve of one of your companions. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature gains temporary hit points equal to the superiority die roll + your Charisma modifier.

options.label: Riposte
options.description: When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction and expend one superiority die to make a melee weapon attack against the creature. If you hit, you add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll.

options.label: Sweeping Attack
options.description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to damage another creature with the same attack. Choose another creature within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. If the original attack roll would hit the second creature, it takes damage equal to the number you roll on your superiority die. The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.

options.label: Trip Attack
options.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to knock the target down. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and if the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you knock the target prone.

options.label: Ambush
options.description: When you make a Dexterity (Stealth) check or an initiative roll, you can expend one superiority die and add the die to the roll, provided you aren’t incapacitated.

options.label: Brace
options.description: When a creature you can see moves into the reach you have with the melee weapon you’re wielding, you can use your reaction to expend one superiority die and make one attack against the creature, using that weapon. If the attack hits, add the superiority die to the weapon’s damage roll.

options.label: Commanding Presence
options.description: When you make a Charisma (Intimidation), a Charisma (Performance), or a Charisma (Persuasion) check, you can expend one superiority die and add the superiority die to the ability check.

options.label: Grappling Strike
options.description: Immediately after you hit a creature with a melee attack on your turn, you can expend one superiority die and then try to grapple the target as a bonus action (see the Player’s Handbook for rules on grappling). Add the superiority die to your Strength (Athletics) check.

options.label: Quick Toss
options.description: As a bonus action, you can expend one superiority die and make a ranged attack with a weapon that has the thrown property. You can draw the weapon as part of making this attack. If you hit, add the superiority die to the weapon’s damage roll.

options.label: Tactical Assessment
options.description: When you make an Intelligence (Investigation), an Intelligence (History), or a Wisdom (Insight) check, you can expend one superiority die and add the superiority die to the ability check.

When you’re within 5 feet of a creature on your turn, you can expend one superiority die and switch places with that creature, provided you spend at least 5 feet of movement and the creature is willing and isn’t incapacitated. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

Roll the superiority die. Until the start of your next turn, you or the other creature (your choice) gains a bonus to AC equal to the number rolled.

options.label: Archery
options.description: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

options.label: Defense
options.description: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

options.label: Dueling
options.description: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

options.label: Great Weapon Fighting
options.description: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

options.label: Protection
options.description: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

options.label: Two-Weapon Fighting
options.description: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

options.label: Blind Fighting
options.description: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn’t behind total cover, even if you’re blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

options.label: Interception
options.description: When a creature you can see hits a target, other than you, within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage the target takes by 1d10 + your proficiency bonus (to a minimum of 0 damage). You must be wielding a shield or a simple or martial weapon to use this reaction.

options.label: Superior Technique
options.description:
You learn one maneuver of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype. If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver’s effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

You gain one superiority die, which is a d6 (this die is added to any superiority dice you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.

options.label: Thrown Weapon Fighting
options.description:
You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.

In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.

options.label: Unarmed Fighting
options.description:
Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren’t wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8.

At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you.

options.label: Armor of Shadows
options.description: You can cast mage armor on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.label: Beast Speech
options.description: You can cast speak with animals at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.label: Beguiling Influence
options.description: You gain proficiency in the Deception and Persuasion skills.

options.label: Devil’s Sight
options.description: You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.

options.label: Eldritch Sight
options.description: You can cast detect magic at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.label: Eyes of the Rune Keeper
options.description: You can read all writing.

options.label: Fiendish Vigor
options.description: You can cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.label: Gaze of Two Minds
options.description: You can use your action to touch a willing humanoid and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. As long as the creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you can use your action on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. While perceiving through the other creature’s senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings.

options.label: Mask of Many Faces
options.description: You can cast disguise self at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.label: Misty Visions
options.description: You can cast silent image at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.label: Eldritch Mind
options.description: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell.

options.label: Charisma
options.description: Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. The spells’ spellcasting ability is Charisma.

options.label: Intelligence
options.description: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20. The spells’ spellcasting ability is Intelligence.

options.label: Careful Spell
options.description: When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the spell’s full force. To do so, you spend 1 sorcery point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell.

options.label: Distant Spell
options.description:
When you cast a spell that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double the range of the spell.

When you cast a spell that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 sorcery point to make the range of the spell 30 feet.

options.label: Empowered Spell
options.description:
When you roll damage for a spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). You must use the new rolls.

You can use Empowered Spell even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

options.label: Extended Spell
options.description: When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

options.label: Heightened Spell
options.description: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 3 sorcery points to give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.

options.label: Quickened Spell
options.description: When you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

options.label: Subtle Spell
options.description: When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to cast it without any somatic or verbal components.

options.label: Twinned Spell
options.description:
When you cast a spell that targets only one creature and doesn’t have a range of self, you can spend a number of sorcery points equal to the spell’s level to target a second creature in range with the same spell (1 sorcery point if the spell is a cantrip).

To be eligible, a spell must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the spell’s current level. For example, magic missile and scorching ray aren’t eligible, but ray of frost and chromatic orb are.

options.label: Seeking Spell
options.description:
If you make an attack roll for a spell and miss, you can spend 2 sorcery points to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll.

You can use Seeking Spell even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

options.label: Transmuted Spell
options.description: When you cast a spell that deals a type of damage from the following list, you can spend 1 sorcery point to change that damage type to one of the other listed types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, thunder.

options.label: Acceptance
options.description:
Characteristics: Those who have gone through a deep and harrowing journey and came to face a truth so difficult that it hurt to accept it—and yet they did it anyways and eventually came to peace with that truth.

Boon Ability: When making a skill check you can choose to add a +5 bonus to the roll. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Envy
options.description:
Characteristics: Someone whose insecurities or past trauma have driven them to desire what others have. This person covets something so much that they’d be willing to do anything to get it, even at the expense of their loved ones.

Boon Ability: Choose an ally creature that you can see and gain proficiency in a skill they have proficiency in. This effect lasts for 1 hour. While you have proficiency in the chosen skill, the ally you copied it from has disadvantage in all checks that use that skill.

options.label: Fearful
options.description:
Characteristics: Through one impactful moment or a slow build over time, this person has been stricken with a deep and overwhelming fear. This fear now clouds their judgment and overrides their emotions—it controls their life.

Boon Ability: If you are hit by an attack while an ally creature is within 5 feet of you, you can choose to have the ally take the damage instead of you. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Forgiveness
options.description:
Characteristics: By accepting their emotions, this person can let go of their anger and frustrations, forgiving those who’ve wronged them and rekindling the damaged relationship.

Boon Ability: When you are hit by an attack, you can choose to cause all subsequent attacks made by the creature to be made at disadvantage. This effect lasts until the end of your next turn. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Hate
options.description:
Characteristics: A person full of hate is blind to the effects their actions can have. To fulfill their vendetta they’re willing to alienate and even hurt those close to them.

Boon Ability: When you make an attack roll or skill check you can choose to change the roll to a 20. If you choose to do this all Charisma, Intelligence, and Wisdom checks are made at disadvantage for the next hour. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Heroic
options.description:
Characteristics: A person who puts fear behind themselves and stands up in a time of need to the very best they can. Whether they fail or not they give everything they can to do what is right.

Boon Ability: When you would fail a Wisdom, Charisma, or Intelligence saving throw, you can instead choose to succeed. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Mercy
options.description:
Characteristics: Those with the power to deal out judgment onto others but have the compassion and understanding to hold back.

Boon Ability: When you make an attack that would drop a creature below zero hit points, you can choose to forgo the damage, making a Charisma skill check with advantage instead. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Shame
options.description:
Characteristics: Devastated by a mistake they’ve made or a circumstance forced on them, this person now hates a part of themselves. This thing feels as if it is out in the open for all to see, and they can’t stand the thought of others judging them for it.

Boon Ability: As a bonus action, all creatures within 60 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to look in your direction until the end of your next turn. The DC for this boon is equal to 10 + your level. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Selfishness
options.description:
Characteristics: Someone whose actions have worsened the lives of those closest to them. A character that, when they could have done the right thing, chose the path for the betterment of themselves over others.

Boon Ability: When you take damage, you can choose to regain 2 hit points for each ally you have within 30 feet of you. When you do so, each ally suffers a number of Necrotic damage equal to the hit points you recovered. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Selfless
options.description:
Characteristics: Above all else, this person puts those around them before themselves. They wish to help the people they care the most about, sometimes to the detriment of their well-being.

Boon Ability: On your turn, you can forgo your action, allowing a character that can see or hear you to take an action or move. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Bestial Awakening (Intelligence)
options.description:
The feral world calls to your soul, howling for you to join it. You can give in to the call and transform into a beast, but the touch of silver bites you more deeply than the sharpest fang.

Beast Skin. You always have the Polymorph spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot or spell components but can target only yourself, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for the spell when you cast it without a spell slot.

Searing Silver. Damage from Silvered Weapons ignores any Resistance or Immunity to damage you have. If you take damage from a Silvered Weapon or touch silver with your bare skin (or its equivalent), you can’t regain Hit Points until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

options.label: Call of the Lonely
options.description:
In the depths of your solitude, and when your hope withered on the branch, you were granted a companion you can call on. You never have to be alone again. This companion is Friendly toward you but is deeply unsettling to your allies.

Never Alone. When no other creature can see you, you can use a Bonus Action to call your companion, which appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. It takes the form of a person or a vague silhouette, and it uses the Doppelganger stat block. It is Friendly toward you and acts as your ally, and it takes its turn on your Initiative in combat. It disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, when you die, or when you use an action to politely dismiss it. When it disappears, it drops anything it was wearing or carrying.

Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Precocious Friend. The companion sometimes appears with trinkets, Cursed Curios*, or other items. It might tell you where it got them, or it might not (GM’s choice). If it took the object from someone who misses it or wants it back, that could create difficulties for you.

Unsettling Presence. While your companion is summoned, both it and you exude a frightful air that unnerves your allies. While the companion is summoned, a creature that isn’t Hostile toward you that starts its turn able to see you or the companion must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the start of its next turn.

options.label: Collector of Stories (Intelligence)
options.description:
You have an insatiable desire to gather the tales of the world. Sometimes, you inadvertently take the story of meeting another person and keep it to yourself, forever.

Gathered Tales. You always have the Legend Lore spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot or spell components, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for the spell when you cast it without a spell slot.

Hoarded Stories. When you use this bargain to cast Legend Lore without a spell slot, a Friendly NPC (the GM chooses) forgets ever meeting you. You can meet them again and attempt to rebuild a relationship, but you forever cause an unsettling discomfort in them. That NPC’s attitude toward you can’t ever improve beyond Indifferent, and you have Disadvantage on all Charisma checks against them.

options.label: Crooked Fortune
options.description:
The crooked fate that governs Druskenvald has taken a liking to you. You can avoid calamity, but you must pay back your good fortune eventually.

Cheat Fate. When you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. When you do so, if you would take half damage on a successful save, you take no damage instead. Once you use Cheat Fate, you can’t use it again until you pay the price (see below).

Delayed Price. After you use Cheat Fate, your next three saving throws have Disadvantage and can’t have Advantage, and you gain 1 Exhaustion level when you succeed on one of the saves. Once you succeed or fail on the third saving throw, you regain the use of Cheat Fate. The powers that govern the warp and weft of fate don’t take kindly to cheating outside their terms—at the GM’s discretion, saving throws made intentionally or without true consequences simply to pay this price painlessly don’t count.

options.label: Cult of Personality
options.description:
You are a force of charm and allure with which to be reckoned. While others fall over themselves to stumble into your good graces, you might find that you end up needing them more than they need you.

Honeyed Words. As a Magic action, you can speak sweet words to a creature within 60 feet of you. The creature has the Charmed condition for 24 hours, until you use this feature again, or until you or your allies deal any damage to the target or force it to make a saving throw. The Charmed target is your ally and follows your commands as long as they don’t require the target to harm itself. If the target carries out a command it finds odious, it makes a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw, ending the condition on itself on a success. Once the condition ends, the target is immune to this feature for 24 hours.

If the target has Immunity to the Charmed condition, it instead has Disadvantage on D20 Tests until the start of your next turn, and you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your level. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Solitary Weakness. If you start your turn with no allies that you can see or hear within 20 feet of you, you lose any Temporary Hit Points you have from any source, and you have Disadvantage on D20 Tests until the start of your next turn.

options.label: Hand of Death
options.description:
Death has no claim on you. In exchange for staying its cold hand without that hand closing, you become a maw through which death feeds on the world around you.

Adamant Endurance. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws.

Cling to Life. When you have 0 Hit Points at the start of your turn, or when you die, you can instead choose to regain a number of Hit Points equal to half your maximum. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again. After using it, whenever you regain Hit Points through any means, you gain only half that amount. Once a Humanoid (other than you) dies within 30 feet of you, you regain the use of this feature, and you can regain Hit Points as normal.

Death Knell. Other creatures within 10 feet of you have Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws, and you can’t restore Hit Points to a creature with 0 Hit Points by any means.

options.label: Might of the Old
options.description:
Ancient and primeval power dwells within the oldest forests of Druskenvald. These powers pour their strength into you but can overwhelm you with their unchanging nature.

Ancient Might. Your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 22, and your Dexterity score decreases by 2.

Primeval Strength. As a Bonus Action, you can call upon the might of the ancients to raise your Strength score to 25 for 1 minute, during which time you deal double damage to objects. Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Pyre’s Price. When you activate Primeval Strength, your skin takes on a bark-like texture, during which time you have Vulnerability to Fire damage. Your skin returns to normal when you finish a Long Rest.

options.label: Self-Serving Sacrifice (Intelligence)
options.description:
You can snatch others from the jaws of death, but your own grip lingers too tightly. The feeling of saving others from suffering fills you with resolve, even as it drains the vigor from those you rescue.

Critical Savior. When a creature within 120 feet of you is subjected to a Critical Hit or is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can use your Reaction to magically switch places with the target. Each of you teleports to the other’s space. Roll a number of d6s equal to half your level. You take Force damage equal to the total rolled, you gain Heroic Inspiration, and your Exhaustion level, if any, is reduced by 1. The target regains Hit Points equal to the total rolled and gains 1 Exhaustion level. You can’t use this feature again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Draining Presence. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, each creature within 100 feet of you loses one Hit Point Die (before spending Hit Dice in the case of finishing a Short Rest).

Final Sacrifice. You can cast True Resurrection using this bargain requiring no spell slot or spell components. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for the spell when you cast it without a spell slot.

When you cast the spell this way, you die, and nothing can prevent it. Your soul is bound to torment the creature you returned to life, and you can’t be raised from the dead by any means. When the creature takes a Long Rest, it must roll a d20 halfway through the rest’s duration. On a 1, your soul takes the form of a Wraith within 100 feet of the creature and tries to kill it. The wraith vanishes after 8 hours, or when it dies. Once the wraith appears, it can’t appear again for 30 days.

options.label: Shrouded Spirit
options.description:
The pall of death drapes over you like the Shroud of Druskenvald. This shroud protects you from the depredations of the Undead, but it draws you ever nearer to their cold embrace.

Inured to Undeath. You have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws against spells and effects created by Undead.

Unholy Appetite. You must consume one pound of raw flesh (it needn’t be fresh) per day or suffer Malnutrition.

Withering Soul. Features that detect your creature type, such as a Paladin’s Divine Sense or the Detect Evil and Good spell, treat you as Undead if your creature type isn’t Undead already.

options.label: Skin of Coffin Nails
options.description:
Your body becomes as coldly unrelenting as iron nails sealing away the dead. You can shrug off staggering punishment, but the waters of the world no longer embrace you, as if spiting your defiance.

Iron Grit. You gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage (your choice when you select this Dark Bargain). You can change the damage type to one of the other options when you finish a Short or Long Rest. When you suffer a Critical Hit from the chosen damage type, it becomes a normal hit instead.

Watery Doom. When you are immersed in water or splashed with at least 1 gallon of water (such as from a bucket or being rained on), your skin tightens and grows rusty until you finish a Short or Long Rest. During that time, your Speed and the time you can hold your breath are halved, and your Resistance to the chosen damage type for Iron Grit becomes Vulnerability instead. At the GM’s discretion, other liquids can also trigger this feature.

options.label: Stilled Hungers
options.description:
Food, drink, and maladies of the flesh have lost their hold over you, but these are the very things that keep a soul vital while in the land of the living. Your mind grows ravenous absent those urges—your thoughts crack with gnawing fears, and your dreams wither into crooked nightmares.

Sated Cravings. Forgoing food and drink doesn’t give you Exhaustion levels. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

Tenuous Psyche. You have Vulnerability to Psychic damage and Disadvantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition. A Calm Emotions spell cast on you suppresses this feature for its duration.

options.label: Unquenchable Fury
options.description:
Anger is a powerful tool. This bargain stokes it into a formidable inferno, but it threatens to consume everything in its path.

Furious Onslaught. As a Bonus Action, or when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can choose to enter a fury. While in this fury, you can make one additional melee attack when you take the Attack action on your turn, and you reduce all damage you take by an amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The fury ends if you have the Incapacitated condition, if you die, or if you end your turn and there are no creatures within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You also regain the use of this feature when you kill a Humanoid.

Red Haze. While you are in a fury, you must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw at the start of each of your turns. On a successful save, you can choose to end your fury or continue it. On a failed save, you no longer make the saving throw at the start of your turns, and you regard the creature nearest to you that you can see or hear as your enemy (if there are multiple, choose one at random). On each of your turns, you must move as close to the creature as possible and take the Attack action, targeting that creature with melee attacks. If you’re unable to get close enough to the creature to attack it, your turn ends after you’ve used up all your available movement. If the creature dies or can no longer be seen or heard by you, the next nearest creature that you can see or hear becomes your new target.

options.label: Wings of Whispers
options.description:
You have been gifted with secrets that you can call upon in the form of ravens and crows to bear you aloft, but at the risk of revealing your own secrets in turn.

Murderous Flight. As a Bonus Action, you can magically gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed (and you can hover) for 10 minutes. During this time, a mass of shadows takes the shape of a murder of crows and ravens (but they aren’t truly creatures). The birds appear in a 20-foot Emanation originating from you and take flight and whirl around you when you fly. Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest, unless you gain 1 Exhaustion level to use it again early.

Whispered Secrets. The birds that appear when you activate Murderous Flight remain and continue to follow you until you finish a Short or Long Rest. While the birds are present, you have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and the birds whisper your secrets into the minds of other creatures, granting them Advantage on Wisdom (Insight or Perception) checks made against you.

options.label: Bloodsworn (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

Cunning. You gain proficiency in your choice of one of the following skills: Deception, Insight, or Intimidation.

Tool of Vengeance. You gain a Common magic item of your choice.

You have been wronged. Now your fate is painted with blood.

Among the Northlanders, no oath is more serious than an oath of vengeance. But when justice cannot be achieved by any other means, a sworn promise to mete out revenge for wrongdoing is the only answer that remains. Those who make such oaths are called Bloodsworn, and their vengeance becomes a tale told by skalds for generations.

As a Bloodsworn, your ultimate goal is revenge upon the one (or ones) who wronged you. Unfortunately, the wrongdoer is beyond your reach, at least for now. This means your plan must be carried out over weeks, months, or even longer. During this time, you’ll no doubt be distracted by other adventures, but your focus demands that you always return to your oath. Bloodsworn must have been wronged or harmed in some way before the gods will accept their blood oath. In most cases, your vengeance will be fatal to your target, but in some situations, other punishments may be more fitting, especially if the wrong you’re avenging doesn’t itself involve a death.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Bloodsworn Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Bloodsworn Goals
d6 Goal
1 I must kill the one who murdered the one I love.
2 I cannot rest until the usurper who killed my jarl is dead by my hands.
3 A crew of scheming charlatans ruined my family’s business. I vow to punish them in ways the law cannot.
4 The power-mad jarl of our lands has destroyed my community. I have a cunning plan to ensure he is overthrown.
5 My trusted shieldmate betrayed me and left me to die. Now I shall return the favor.
6 I was shamed by the false words of another. I will deliver vengeance tenfold upon my accuser.

options.label: Bloodsworn (Level 5)
options.description:
Lesser Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

Enemy of My Enemy. You’ve made an ally, a person who is also sworn to oppose your enemy. They have granted you an underground hideout from which to conduct your campaign of vengeance.

Wrath. You can cast Wrathful Smite, using your choice of INT, WIS, or CHA as your spellcasting ability score. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

Cunning. You gain proficiency in your choice of one of the following skills: Deception, Insight, or Intimidation.

Tool of Vengeance. You gain a Common magic item of your choice.

options.label: Bloodsworn (Level 11)
options.description:
Greater Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

Tenacity. You can resist effects that would slow your oath from being carried out. If you begin your turn with the Frightened, Incapacitated, Paralyzed, or Stunned condition, you may choose to end one of those conditions. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

options.label: Bloodsworn (Level 17)
options.description:
Superior Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

Dire Oath. When you complete a Long Rest, name a specific creature you swore your oath against or who stands in the way of you completing your oath. For the next 24 hours, that creature is marked by your dire oath. While the dire oath lasts, you have Advantage on all attack rolls made against that creature, and Advantage on skill checks made to locate or learn about that creature.

After you use this feature, you must wait 7 days before you can use it again.

options.label: Cursemarked (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefits.

Tides of Fate [1–3, Saving Throws]. Your Speed is reduced by 10 feet. When this occurs, the Speed of another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you increases by 10 feet. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

Greater Sacrifice. When your Tides of Fate is triggered, you can choose to reduce your Speed to 0 until the start of your next turn. If you do so, in addition to the normal benefit, the chosen creature does not provoke opportunity attacks and ignores Difficult Terrain until the end of your next turn. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

You bear the brunt of a curse of ill luck, and it’ll get worse before the end.

Northlanders place great faith in the existence of luck. The gods can bestow good fortune upon the faithful, and honorable actions can directly lead to successful endeavors. Likewise, disreputable behavior can bring failure not only to you, but to future generations of your family.

You are one of the unfortunates, chosen by fate or the gods to suffer from ill luck wherever you go. Perhaps you earned this curse through dishonor, oathbreaking, or cowardice. You might bear misfortune as a virtual heirloom, passed down to you by a disreputable ancestor. Other cursemarked are victims of witch’s curses or similar supernatural effects. Whatever the reason, you can’t seem to catch a break.

Strangely, the presence of a Cursemarked can often bring good fortune to those nearby. As long as your friends are willing to put up with your occasional mishaps, the long-term benefit might well be worthwhile. Meanwhile, however, the cursemarked searches for some way to atone for their misdeeds, real or imagined, knowing such a road will be long and will certainly grow worse before the end. Yet when the hand of fortune is turned against you, what else can you do?

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Cursemarked Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Cursemarked Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will atone for my dishonor by returning a sacred relic to a distant tomb.
2 I can only lift this curse by clearing the name of an ancestor falsely accused of murder.
3 I must prove my courage to the gods by defeating a tribe of marauding giants.
4 I will invoke Freyr’s blessing by forging peace between two warring clans.
5 To end this curse, I shall endure trials of my honor, my valor, and my selflessness.
6 I must convince Wotan himself to intervene and convince the Norns to reshape my fate.
Cursemarked Milestone Rules

Cursemarked milestones work a bit differently than those of other character threads. The milestone features described below trigger when you roll for specific mechanics (saving throws, ability checks or attack roll, depending on the feature) and get a result within the range of numbers indicated in the bracket for each milestone. Milestone features never overlap, so if you trigger a feature, you can’t trigger another until the start of your next turn after the duration of the previous one expires.

options.label: Cursemarked (Level 5)
options.description:
Lesser Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone feature benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

Burden’s Shield [1–5, Saving Throws, Ability Checks]. Your AC is reduced by 2. When this occurs, the AC of another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you increases by 2. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

Greater Sacrifice. When your Burden’s Shield is triggered, you can choose to reduce your AC by 4 instead of 2. If you do so, the AC of the chosen creature increases by 4 (instead of 2), or you can choose for it to receive the benefit of the Tide of Fate’s Greater Sacrifice. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

options.label: Cursemarked (Level 11)
options.description:

When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone feature benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

Threads Entwined [1–7, Saving Throws, Ability Checks, Attack Rolls]. You can’t take Bonus Actions or Reactions until the end of your next turn. When this occurs, another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you can immediately use its Reaction to take the Dash, Help, or Hide action, or make a single weapon attack against a target in range.

Greater Sacrifice. When your Threads Entwined is triggered, you can instead choose to do nothing this turn besides move. If you’ve already taken your action this turn, you instead forgo your action on your next turn. If you do so, the chosen creature can take one additional action on its next turn, except the Magic action, or it can receive the benefit of one of the previous milestone feature’s Greater Sacrifices. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

options.label: Cursemarked (Level 17)
options.description:
Superior Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone feature benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

Two-Edged Gift [1–9, Saving Throws, Ability Checks, Attack Rolls]. Your weapon attacks and spells deal half their normal damage until the end of your next turn. During this time, the first time a creature of your choice within 30 feet of you deals damage with a weapon or spell, that creature deals maximum damage.

Greater Sacrifice. When your Two-Edged Gift is triggered, you can instead choose deal no damage with weapons and spells until the end of your next turn. If you do so, the next weapon or spell attack the chosen creature makes before the end of its next turn is automatically a Critical Hit, or it can receive the benefit of one of the previous milestone feature’s Greater Sacrifice. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Greater Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone feature benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

Threads Entwined [1–7, Saving Throws, Ability Checks, Attack Rolls]. You can’t take Bonus Actions or Reactions until the end of your next turn. When this occurs, another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you can immediately use its Reaction to take the Dash, Help, or Hide action, or make a single weapon attack against a target in range.

Greater Sacrifice. When your Threads Entwined is triggered, you can instead choose to do nothing this turn besides move. If you’ve already taken your action this turn, you instead forgo your action on your next turn. If you do so, the chosen creature can take one additional action on its next turn, except the Magic action, or it can receive the benefit of one of the previous milestone feature’s Greater Sacrifices. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Lesser Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone feature benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

Burden’s Shield [1–5, Saving Throws, Ability Checks]. Your AC is reduced by 2. When this occurs, the AC of another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you increases by 2. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

Greater Sacrifice. When your Burden’s Shield is triggered, you can choose to reduce your AC by 4 instead of 2. If you do so, the AC of the chosen creature increases by 4 (instead of 2), or you can choose for it to receive the benefit of the Tide of Fate’s Greater Sacrifice. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefits.

Tides of Fate [1–3, Saving Throws]. Your Speed is reduced by 10 feet. When this occurs, the Speed of another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you increases by 10 feet. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

Greater Sacrifice. When your Tides of Fate is triggered, you can choose to reduce your Speed to 0 until the start of your next turn. If you do so, in addition to the normal benefit, the chosen creature does not provoke opportunity attacks and ignores Difficult Terrain until the end of your next turn. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

options.label: Explorer (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

Celebrity Explorer. You receive a 30% discount on lodging, supplies, and food from innkeepers, merchants, and proprietors, and it’s common for them to offer you things for free.

Explorer’s Aptitude. Your travels instill you with new knowledge. You gain proficiency in your choice of one of the following skills: Athletics, History, or Perception.

Glory lies just over the horizon. Time to find it.

Explorers occupy an unusual place in Northlands society. Though revered for their courage, they rarely find a comfortable place in a community. Driven by wanderlust, curiosity, boredom, or a simple inability to relate to civilized folks, the Explorer spends most of their time in the wilderness. Some climb mountains, others set sail for lost lands, and still others delve through dark tunnels beneath the earth. For an Explorer, the greatest treasure awaits beyond the next hill.

Whether by choice or by fate, you follow the path less traveled. Perhaps you’re a rugged seafarer or mountaineer seeking discoveries in the wild. Other Explorers are treasure hunters, royal mapmakers, or seekers of truth. You might be an exile, outlaw, or iconoclast, who simply can’t get along with others. Or you might be driven by vision or prophecy to forsake hearth and home for the unknown.

 Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Explorer Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

GM Note. This thread brings flavorful Northlands themes into a campaign and can be taken up by characters of any class. However, it can tread on the toes of any Rangers in the party. Consult with your Ranger players before allowing a character to take on this thread to make sure no feelings will be hurt.

Explorer Goals
d6 Goal
1 I shall find a route through the Bloodfjord Mountains never before traveled by mortals.
2 To avert Ragnarok, I must carry a prophecy to a far-flung land.
3 My mother died searching for the headwaters of the Tearstain River. I shall complete her quest.
4 I seek a sapling of the World Tree, rumored to be growing on a tiny island in the Nieder Strait.
5 Once I decipher the ancient map I hold, I’ll delve into the depths of Narvegr Maw.
6 The Frozen Palace of the last Hyperborean lies somewhere in the Bleak Expanse. I’ll find it and return with his icy crown.

options.label: Explorer (Level 5)
options.description:
Lesser Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

Traversal Expert. You have a knack for finding easy paths through the environment. You may use your Bonus Action to move your Speed. During this movement, you ignore Difficult Terrain and have Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to climb, jump, or swim. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Scout’s Awareness. You have a preternatural sense that allows you to avoid dangers in your surroundings. For 1 hour, you and each ally within 30 feet who can see you have Advantage on saving throws to resist the effects of nonmagical traps and hazards. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

options.label: Explorer (Level 11)
options.description:
Greater Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain one of the following benefits.

Ennobled. A monarch has recognized your achievements as an Explorer in their or other territories by granting you a noble title, which comes with a moderately sized estate. You have Advantage on Charisma checks with anyone who would be impressed or intimidated by your title. You also can avoid punishment for minor infractions, though if you abuse this, your title might be revoked.

Wayfarer’s Steps. You can never become lost by nonmagical means and can always retrace your steps. Additionally, as a Bonus Action, you can take the Dash action and command up to 4 willing creatures who can hear you to use their Reaction to immediately take a Dash action. Neither you nor your allies trigger Opportunity Attacks while moving in this way. Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

One With the Land. You may study the land from a good vantage point (such as a high position or advantageous overlook) for 1 minute and ask a question concerning the natural world or locations within 5 miles. options.label: Fatebound (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one the following benefits.

Dream Gift. A god, Norn, or other powerful being has given you a gift in a dream. When you awoke, you had a Common magic item of the GM’s choice that may aid you.

Fate’s Blessing. Once per day, while you are Bloodied, you can use your Reaction to get Advantage on a saving throw.

Your fate is written. Make it glorious.

Many warriors loudly boast of their desire for a noble death or an honorable end in battle, to thus earn a seat in the great hall of Valhalla. These boasts are but hopeful wishes since most individuals never see the path of their future. You, however, are not most individuals. You have been blessed, or perhaps cursed, with the knowledge of your end, though this knowledge doesn’t tell you if you succeed or fail in the circumstance surrounding your death. You might know you will die facing a dark warlord, but you don’t know if you will defeat her. Despite this, the Norns have given you a rare opportunity. The knowledge you possess will help you ensure your death is worthy of the sagas.

Some of those who are Fatebound are marked from birth. Others learn of their fate from seers, shamans, or divine visions. Some heroes earn this thread after engaging in activities that move the gods or the Norns to reward them with such a potent end.

Fatebound and Death. Keep in mind that having this thread may mean you can’t die before your fated time, but it doesn’t mean you will reach that point whole and healthy. While your fate is inevitable, luck alone determines your condition when you meet that end. Do you lead a glorious charge across the battlefield? Or are you left guarding the baggage? Has every confrontation leading up to your end prepared you to defeat your ultimate foe? Or has a lifetime of avoidance left you ill-prepared?

If a Fatebound PC is killed before their time, and magical resurrection is not an option, a GM could instead choose for them to be injured in a significant way—such as the loss of a limb or eye. These injuries should not be able to be healed without high-level magic. Alternatively, perhaps they lose one of their powerful magical items instead of their lives, or they might suffer a level of Exhaustion until they reach their next milestone. The GM and player should agree on this complication.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Fatebound Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

GM Note: The Fatebound is an unusual thread in that its final milestone specifically describes the manner in which a character might meet with a permanent death, likely as part of the final accomplishment of their goal, and then empowers the PCs’ allies as a reward. Most importantly, this thread should be something the player consciously selects.

Fatebound Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will die only after finding and facing the mightiest dragon in the land.
2 I will be slain by Utgard-Loki while attempting to thwart his plan to slay the gods.
3 To defend my people from invasion, I pledge to pay any price, including my own life.
4 I shall search for and find a fabled lost treasure, but I will die in the process.
5 I will rise to become the North’s greatest reaver, then perish battling the World Serpent.
6 I seek the truth behind the fall of Nordheim, though it will cost my life to learn it.

options.label: Fatebound (Level 5)
options.description:
Lesser Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

Strength of Wyrd. While you are Bloodied, once per turn you may add your Proficiency Bonus to a damage roll. You may use this damage bonus a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Enduring Wyrd. When you take damage, you may use your Reaction to gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You cannot use this feature again until you complete a Short or Long Rest.

Doom Delayed. When you would be killed, you may instead declare yourself as Stable with 0 Hit Points. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Knight of Fate. You have become a legend in a territory, and the monarch there has knighted you, granting you holdings that will revert back to the monarchy upon your death. You have Advantage on Charisma-based checks with the people of this land and are frequently showered with minor gifts and favors there.

options.label: Fatebound (Level 17)
options.description:
Superior Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefits.

Last Act of Fate. At a moment you have predetermined to be the time when you are to die, when you are reduced 0 Hit Points or killed outright, you may (no action required) instead set your Hit Points to 1. You lose any detrimental conditions, and any harmful effects on you are ended immediately. Until the end of your next turn, you gain Advantage on all attack rolls and ability checks, you have Immunity to all damage and conditions (and other effects at the GM’s discretion), and you add your character level to all damage rolls.

At the end of your next turn, you die and can never be restored to life.

Glorious End. If you achieve your destiny in a way that earns you a seat in Valhalla (or some other appropriate afterlife), the allies who witness your death have Advantage on all d20 rolls for 24 hours as they are inspired by your heroism.

options.label: Herald (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefits.

Storyteller’s Knack. You learn three languages of your choice.

Performer’s Reward. If you have at least 3 days of downtime between adventures, you can earn GP equal to 10 times your character level by performing your stories in taverns, on the street, or for powerful patrons. Additional downtime events don’t increase this reward.

Your stories don’t just recount events . . . they shape history.

Storytellers are revered in the Northlands. Whether a skald sharing tales around a fire, a lore keeper gathering sagas to pass down the generations, or a grizzled reaver frightening young warriors by recalling harrowing battles, the tradition of collecting stories is respected across nearly all cultures in the region. As a Herald, you are a proud, if temporary, part of this tradition, driven by a need to spread stories during your travels to accomplish a specific end.

Perhaps your stories encourage downtrodden karls to rise up against their cruel jarl, warn a region about an approaching invasion, or convince warriors to join your cause. Part skald, part herald, part envoy, you will use your tales and stories to sway the minds of your audience and help shape the world.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Herald Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

GM Note. This thread brings flavorful Northlands themes into a campaign and can be taken up by characters of any class. However, it can tread on the toes of any Bards in the party. Consult with your Bard players before allowing a character to take on this thread to make sure no feelings will be hurt.

Herald Goals
d6 Goal
1 The feared invasion from Jotunheim approaches, and the country must be warned.
2 By telling the sagas, I will gather support for the greatest raid the North has ever launched.
3 My tales flatter Thor and Wotan in the hope they will support our struggle against the forces of Chernobog and Angrboda.
4 I spread the word of the great crusade to eradicate the darkness beneath Tanserhall. Heed my call!
5 I seek a lost treasure of Hyperborea, and by spreading tales of similar treasures, I hope to find a path to a hidden vault.
6 To rouse the people against their evil king, I shall assemble an array of sorrowful tales of corruption that cannot be ignored.

options.label: Herald (Level 5)
options.description:

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

Enthralling Speaker. You gain proficiency in the Performance skill. If you are already proficient, you instead gain Expertise. Additionally, while performing before an audience, you can cast either Charm Person or Suggestion as part of your performance without requiring somatic or material components. Use Charisma as your spellcasting ability score. After casting one of these spells using this feature, you can’t use the feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

After you spend at least 10 minutes telling an inspiring story or legend, choose either one creature who can hear you, or up to three creatures. You can’t select yourself as a target. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until for 7 days.

Depending on the number of targets, creatures can receive one of the following.

Luck Boon (Three Targets). Once before the next Long Rest, a target can expend their boon to gain Advantage on a saving throw, attack roll, or ability check.

Wyrd Boon (One Target). Once before their next Long Rest, if the target does not succeed on a saving throw or attack roll, they can choose to succeed instead. An attack roll succeeding in this way results in the minimum needed to succeed (not a Critical Hit, for example).

Song of Matrimony. A member of the royal family in a particular land has fallen in love with you and your performances, and the feeling is mutual. You are engaged to marry into the royal family.

options.label: Legend Hunter (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

Predator’s Mark. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to track creatures, and on a failed check it only takes you half the time to reacquire the tracks (5 minutes in a confined area, or half an hour outdoors).

Neither storm nor night nor bloody fang shall slow your relentless pursuit.

Hunting is as old as the Northlands itself. From volcanic peaks to frigid fens and aurora-bathed glaciers, the tales of hunters are sung alongside those of heroes and gods. While some may hunt for survival or vengeance, you are different. You are a hunter to be feared, as you hunt for the thrill of the chase and the glory of victory.

As a Legend Hunter, you may have been chosen by the Norns, blessed by a god, or forged in trials of blood and grift. No matter how you come to it, your extraordinary search for greater and greater prey sets you apart from those who hunt merely for survival. You do not merely forge trails; you craft sagas. You do not merely slay beasts; you end legends to become a legend.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Legend Hunter Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Legend Hunter Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will prove my valor by tracking down and slaying a legendary monster that has been destroying villages.
2 I hunt for a mythical two-headed jotun somewhere in the Bleak Expanse.
3 Besting a great dragon in its lair shall be my ultimate victory.
4 I will go beneath the waves to bring low the mother of all krakens.
5 I will bring back the head of Fenris.
6 My legend will be assured when I go among the roots of Yggdrasil to slay Nidhogg.

options.label: Legend Hunter (Level 5)
options.description:
Lesser Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

Unclouded Sight. Your honed senses let you ignore obscurement caused by weather, such as rain, snow, or fog. This includes magical clouds and weather effects, such as Fog Cloud and Sleet Storm, but not Darkness.

Reliable Senses. After failing an Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Perception), or Wisdom (Survival) check, you can reroll the check and take the higher result. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

options.description:
Superior Milestone Feature

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

Legend Breaker. When you hit a creature that has Legendary Resistance or Legendary Actions, you can choose to forgo dealing damage to force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Wisdom modifier and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the target becomes unable use its Legendary Resistance or its Legendary Actions. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

The Ultimate Favor. You performed a service for a powerful healer, who was caught in an animal trap set by another hunter. In return, they have offered to cast a single spell of healing of 6th to 9th level on you or a creature of your choice, at a time of your choosing, even if this puts them at great risk. This should be a spell that heals, regenerates, resurrects, or that removes conditions or curses.

Finish the Fight. When you cause a creature to become Bloodied, your next attack that hits it becomes a Critical Hit. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Lesser Milestone Feature

Unclouded Sight. Your honed senses let you ignore obscurement caused by weather, such as rain, snow, or fog. This includes magical clouds and weather effects, such as Fog Cloud and Sleet Storm, but not Darkness.

Reliable Senses. After failing an Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Perception), or Wisdom (Survival) check, you can reroll the check and take the higher result. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Least Milestone Feature

Predator’s Mark. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to track creatures, and on a failed check it only takes you half the time to reacquire the tracks (5 minutes in a confined area, or half an hour outdoors).

options.label: Sworn Huskarl (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

Jarl’s Authority. The authority granted you by your loyal service can sway the opinions of others. Before rolling an Intimidation or Persuasion check to influence someone who knows and respects (or fears) your ruler, you can choose to treat the d20 roll as if you’d rolled a natural 15. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

You carry out the will of your king, no matter the risk.

You have pledged your loyalty to an important personage, promising to guard them or travel across the Northlands in their service, risking danger as you seek to accomplish a great task. In the past, it was expected that a huskarl would swear to serve a lord for life or until they were dismissed. While jarls still take huskarls in that way, they also accept the service of huskarls on a temporary basis, to perform specific deeds or until certain threats are dealt with. These are the types of huskarls described in this thread.

The sworn huskarl enjoys a position of respect within their lord’s retinue. More than a mere bodyguard, you are a trusted agent acting on your ruler’s behalf. You carry some of their authority with you, but that also comes with the responsibility to act in ways they would approve. Sworn huskarls who bring shame to their jarl don’t remain in service for long.

A jarl takes on a new huskarl with a simple ceremony in which the huskarl swears an oath in the longhouse before a gathering of other members of the felag. During the oath-swearing, the goals or timeframe for the service are mentioned (unless the jarl keeps your mission a secret). Traditionally, your reasons for serving are respect for the lord, payment, or power. However, in some cases your oath may hold a secret. Perhaps you made it under threat of violence or under false pretenses. Or maybe your lord doesn’t deserve such loyalty. You might serve under protest or with your own goal that’s unknown to your ruler.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Sworn Huskarl Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Sworn Huskarl Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will find my king’s long-lost child so that my kingdom will have a true heir.
2 My queen depends on me to find and slay the pretender who claims a blood right to her throne.
3 I must root out a hidden sect of the Cult of Ragnarok that grows within my jarl’s land.
4 Giant raiding parties threaten the land. My jarl calls upon me to destroy them and make the land safe once more.
5 I can only earn my freedom by finding the stolen crown of my sadistic monarch.
6 I serve only until I can discover a way to overthrow this corrupt king, who took the throne through dark sorcery.

All creatures in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier + your Proficiency Bonus). On a failure, a creature takes 2d8 Bludgeoning damage and 3d8 Cold damage, and has the Prone condition; on a success, the creature takes half as much damage and doesn’t have the Prone condition.
